criteria.text: Identifies the conflict between the 20-day claim notice period in SPA Section 9.7 and the 45-day period in Escrow Clause 5.2, and recommends the Buyer works to the shorter 20-day period or aligns the documents.

Identifies that the core platform was developed by contractor Thornbury Analytics Ltd without a written IP assignment, so the Company may not own it, and recommends obtaining a confirmatory assignment as a condition to Closing.
Calculates the long-stop date as 15 September 2026 (90 days after signing on 17 June 2026) and identifies that expected clearance on 29 September 2026 falls after it, recommending an extension.
Identifies that the warranty cap in SPA Section 8.3 is stated as $15,937,500 but 15% of the $85,000,000 Purchase Price is $12,750,000, i.e. the stated figure is wrong.

Identifies that the MAC carve-outs (general economic, industry-wide and pandemic changes) contain no 'disproportionate effect' exception, so the Buyer bears those risks even where the Company is disproportionately affected, and recommends adding one.
Explains how 'material adverse effect' could be read narrowly or broadly and what each reading means for the Buyer's walk-away right.
Shows the arithmetic for the cap (15% x $85,000,000 = $12,750,000) and flags the discrepancy with the stated $15,937,500.
Gives a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause number) for every issue or finding.
